solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Union money's invested in a fine city, ultimately like Cologne

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go into the middle of the rest
ultimately points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a day' means per
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
U is a standard abbreviation for union
M is short for money
last letter of city

explanation.surface: Union funds are being poured into a fashionable city, which ends up rather like Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: PER, F and Y make the outer shell, with U and M slipped in between F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a scent, so something like it is perfumy, smelling of perfume.

clue.text: Relative pressure shown up in letters from abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sister is a relative
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Some family pressure is revealed in letters sent from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from abroad' sounds like foreign mail, but it means Greek alphabet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so its plural names foreign letters.

clue.text: Ring dated chaps on land wanting introductions

indicators.note: lacking their introductions means each word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: chaps are men
land as in a piece of ground

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned call to surround men standing on some ground that has no proper introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' belongs with the definition: the word is Shakespearean. Both chunks lose their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enround is an archaic verb meaning to encircle or surround, exactly as to ring something.

clue.text: Rather fat seaman in launch

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: a product's launch is its rollout
AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor carrying a bit of extra weight takes part in a boat launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists rollabout as an adjective for someone plump, pudgy and rolling in gait.

clue.text: Type of algae, great deal loaded by porter in America

indicators.note: in tells us the preceding string sits inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: US, the United States
a lot is a great deal
loaded means wealthy
porter is a dark ale

explanation.surface: An algal species is shipped in bulk to America, carried by a railway porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a baggage handler; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulotrichales is an order of green algae, so a name for one type of algae.

clue.text: School teams value degree

indicators.note: to school is to drill or train, putting things into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
to value is to rate

explanation.surface: A school judges how good its sports teams are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' reads as a noun heading the sentence; it is a verb telling us to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterate is a master's degree, the qualification above a bachelor's.

clue.text: Echo remark initially about part of Koran? It's well-proportioned

indicators.note: about means going around something, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a remark is a comment
a sura is a chapter of the Koran
Echo is E in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A remark about a passage of the Koran echoes round, and is judged balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Echo letter belongs at the end even though the clue names it first; 'initially' is best read as pointing to the remark coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: Commensurate means in proportion to or corresponding in size, so it fits well-proportioned.

clue.text: An Indian measure is expensive, no end of loot

indicators.note: having no end of means one specific letter goes

blocks.note: something expensive costs a lot
the end of loot is its last letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: An Indian measure of something valuable costs dearly, though the plunder never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The T is taken out of the middle of COSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A coss (or kos) is an Indian unit of distance of roughly two miles.

clue.text: Fly on after Cuba

indicators.note: after sends the word before it to second place, behind the country's code

blocks.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
in cricket, the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a flight on from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about travel; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleg is a horsefly, a biting fly.

clue.text: Preposterous game — it's a fiddle

indicators.note: preposterous literally means before-after, putting the last part first

blocks.note: darts is a pub game

explanation.surface: Someone calls a game absurd and a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a cheat; it is a violin, and a Strad is a Stradivarius.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is a violin made by Stradivari, and fiddle is the informal word for a violin.

clue.text: Fox is only half-seen before reaching high-street store

indicators.note: only half of each word is seen, so its front half is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written; only its back half is kept
taken as written; only its back half is kept
Boots is a chain of chemists found on every British high street

explanation.surface: A fox, barely glimpsed, slinks past on its way to a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only' does double duty: it is read with 'half-seen' as the instruction, and it is also one of the two words halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A slyboots is a cunning person, and a fox is a byword for a crafty schemer.

clue.text: Pros back for snub in Edinburgh

indicators.note: back means read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: in Scots, loon can mean a harlot, so pros (prostitutes) are loons

explanation.surface: Professionals return to give someone the cold shoulder in Scotland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Edinburgh' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: To snool is Scots for to snub, cow or keep someone down.

clue.text: Amphibian awfully lax catching nothing by chance

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters come out disordered
catching means holding something within

blocks.note: taken as written for the shuffle
O is zero, nothing
deciding by lot is deciding by chance

explanation.surface: A salamander, terribly relaxed, catches nothing except by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander, an amphibian that keeps its larval form.

clue.text: Radiation measurement test follows three notes

blocks.note: do, si and me are notes of the sol-fa scale
to test is to try

explanation.surface: A radiation measurement test comes after three musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosimetry is the science of measuring absorbed doses of radiation.

clue.text: Pieces for one only heard

indicators.note: heard means we go by how a word sounds when spoken

blocks.note: only means solely

explanation.surface: Pieces for a single performer, only ever heard rather than seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Soli is the plural of solo, a musical piece for a single performer.

clue.text: Poet's faint with piercing alarm signal

definitions.note: faint here is a noun, matching the verbal noun

indicators.note: piercing means going into something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: an alarm sounding is its signal
W is short for with

explanation.surface: A poet passes out as an alarm pierces the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' wants to be a definition of wounding; it is the instruction to put W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Swound is an old poetic form of swoon, so swounding is fainting in poetry.

clue.text: Endless rubbish, it's also known as Buddhist literature

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: tripe is nonsense
taken as written
aka is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses Buddhist scripture as endless nonsense with another name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripitaka, the Pali canon, is the three-part body of Buddhist scripture.

clue.text: Inquire?!

definitions.note: a noun: a question mark or query

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin imperative, used in English for ask or seek
second meaning: a query, the thing the question mark stands for

explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation is part of the clue: the question mark is itself the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaere is Latin for seek, used in English to introduce a doubtful point, and as a noun for a query.

clue.text: Turkish officer's question and answer followed by another boring mosque leader

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the repeated pair goes inside

blocks.note: Q and A are the abbreviations
an imam leads prayers in a mosque
a second question and answer

explanation.surface: A Turkish official holds a question-and-answer session, followed by a tedious one from the imam.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition is 'is' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A qaimaqam was an Ottoman district governor or lieutenant, a Turkish official.

clue.text: Odd fish in dam as before

blocks.note: a weir is a small dam
do, short for ditto, means as before

explanation.surface: A strange fish turns up in a dam again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd fish' is an idiom for a strange person, not a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is an eccentric person, which is what a weirdo is.

clue.text: Social security payment, initially no charge

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: a giro was a British benefit payment by cheque
first letter of no

explanation.surface: A benefit payment arrives, and at first there is no fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a fee; it is a heraldic charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a giron (gyron) is a triangular charge, a figure placed on a shield.

clue.text: One politician leaving Mexican port is a Central American

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the word

blocks.note: a means one
MP, Member of Parliament
Tampico is a port on Mexico's Gulf coast

explanation.surface: A politician quits a Mexican port and turns out to be from Central America.
explanation.definitionFit: Tico is the informal name for a Costa Rican, a Central American.

clue.text: Natives mostly boasted sole supply

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter
read as an adverb, supply means flexibly, so the letters bend into another order

blocks.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast
taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Local people bragged that they mostly provided the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun; it is the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A Creole is a person born in the Caribbean or Louisiana of settler descent, so a native.

clue.text: Old impostor useless when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the word counts by its sound

blocks.note: idle means useless or futile

explanation.surface: An old fraud is no use when giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In obsolete use an idol was a counterfeit or impostor, a false likeness.

clue.text: Will's affair in California upset Sue

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled

blocks.note: CA is the state abbreviation
taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A man called Will has an affair in California, and Sue is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Shakespeare, so this is his sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses cause for a matter or business in hand, an affair.

clue.text: Might once used by Maurice on violent thug

indicators.note: violent means wild and disordered

blocks.note: Mo is a short form of Maurice
taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Might was once used by a man named Maurice against a violent thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like strength; it is the past of may.
explanation.definitionFit: Mought is an obsolete form of might, the past tense of may.

clue.text: Windows foremost in operating computers, usually Chinese units

indicators.note: foremost picks the leading letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of these three words
the li is a Chinese unit of length

explanation.surface: Windows comes first in operating computers, as a rule, even in Chinese firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' looks like the software; it is round openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculi are round windows, such as the eye-shaped openings in a dome.

clue.text: Greek character longs to get Playboy pics?

blocks.note: nu is a Greek letter
to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A Greek man longs to get hold of Playboy pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudies are photos or films of naked people, the kind of picture Playboy runs; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: See about top of mountain covered by trees

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter
about means going round something else

blocks.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see
first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: Take a look at a mountain summit hidden under woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's see, as in the cathedral city of ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmy means full of elm trees, so wooded.

clue.text: Incomplete school pack

indicators.note: incomplete means the word falls one letter short

blocks.note: Stowe is an English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil packs a school bag but leaves it half done.
explanation.walkthrough: STOWE is a fee-paying boarding school in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or store things away.

clue.text: Black lead in tawdry play forgetting lines

indicators.note: forgetting means leaving something out
play means move freely, so the letters shift about

blocks.note: taken as written
RY, railway: railway lines

explanation.surface: A black-clad lead actor in a cheap play forgets his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black lead' looks like a theatre role; it is graphite.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadt (or wad) is a dialect word for graphite, also called black lead.

clue.text: Question with difficulty maids in S American trees

blocks.note: QU is short for question
as in 'ill afford': with difficulty
an aia (ayah) is an Indian nursemaid

explanation.surface: Questioning maids proves hard work among South American trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The quillaia is a Chilean soapbark tree, so these are South American trees.

clue.text: Scots own guards weak in battle

indicators.note: guards means surrounds and protects

blocks.note: ain is Scots for own
a lame excuse is a weak one

explanation.surface: Scottish soldiers protect their own weak members during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of the decisive Second World War battle of 1942.

clue.text: Unruly youngster tearing around certainly puffed

indicators.note: running around something encloses it

blocks.note: a Ted is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth rebel
OK means certainly, sure

explanation.surface: An unruly youngster runs about, certainly out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffed' looks like breathless; it means smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To toke is to draw on a joint, so toked means puffed on one.

clue.text: Friendly relations leaving area infested with insects

indicators.note: leaving means the letter departs

blocks.note: amity is friendship
A is short for area

explanation.surface: Friendly neighbours move out of a place overrun with bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mity means full of mites, the tiny arachnids loosely called insects.

clue.text: One wouldn't laugh at engaging upper-class girl, for instance

indicators.note: engaging means taking hold of, so the word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
gel is the posh pronunciation of girl
as means for instance, as in 'cities as Paris'

explanation.surface: A sour person would not laugh at an upper-class girl, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: An agelast is someone who never laughs, from the Greek for not laughing.
